text:
## Observations

1. An operation exchanges a full block of X zeros with a full block of Y ones. A full block can also slide past individual bits of its own kind, since that leaves the binary string identical.
2. In a representation that keeps full blocks and residual runs, each full block can move left to the gap immediately after the last residual run of the opposite bit to its left, or to the leading gap if no such run exists.
3. When scanning left to right, a new bit can extend the last residual run if it has the same bit and the trailing gap is empty. A residual run that reaches its block size becomes one full block.
4. Appending exactly one block’s worth of a bit restores the previous residual runs and adds one full block to the gap after the last opposite residual run. Appending a full zero block and a full one block therefore has the same effect in either order.
5. The position of the most recent residual run of either bit can be maintained in constant time when adding or removing the last run.

## Solution sketch

1. “An operation exchanges a full block of X zeros with a full block of Y ones. A full block can also slide past individual bits of its own kind, since that leaves the binary string identical.”

   Represent a scanned prefix by an ordered list of residual runs, with a gap before the first run and after every run. Each gap stores two counts, one for full zero blocks and one for full one blocks. Interpret each gap in a fixed order, with zero blocks before one blocks. Either order is reachable using the allowed swaps. Start with an empty list and an empty leading gap.

2. “When scanning left to right, a new bit can extend the last residual run if it has the same bit and the trailing gap is empty. A residual run that reaches its block size becomes one full block.”

   Scan the string one bit at a time. Extend the last run when the stated condition holds. Otherwise, add a new run of length one with an empty gap after it. If the affected run reaches length X for zeros or Y for ones, remove it and its empty following gap, then place the resulting full block as described in the next step. This also handles a block size of one, where each bit of that kind immediately becomes a full block.

3. “In a representation that keeps full blocks and residual runs, each full block can move left to the gap immediately after the last residual run of the opposite bit to its left, or to the leading gap if no such run exists.”

   Place a newly formed block by incrementing its count in that destination gap. The block can reach it by crossing same-bit residual runs and full blocks of either kind. This maintains the rule that each full block is in the first gap after the most recent opposite residual run to its left. Consequently, the trailing gap after a residual run can hold only blocks of the opposite bit. Consecutive residual runs of the same bit are always separated by a gap containing an opposite full block, since a run would otherwise have been extended. Every update represents a transformation allowed by the problem.

4. “Appending exactly one block’s worth of a bit restores the previous residual runs and adds one full block to the gap after the last opposite residual run. Appending a full zero block and a full one block therefore has the same effect in either order.”

   If the appended bits extend a residual run, its length wraps around once at the block size and returns to its starting length. When the run is temporarily removed, any preceding run of the same bit is still separated by an opposite full block, so the remaining bits recreate the removed run in its original place. If the bits start a new run, that run reaches the block size and disappears. In either case, the residual runs and gap counts return to their previous values except for the one added block. The destinations for a full zero block and a full one block depend only on the residual runs, so the two additions commute. This proves that a swap anywhere in the string preserves the final representation. The scan has the same state before the swapped substring, reaches the same state after it, and processes the same suffix.

5. “The position of the most recent residual run of either bit can be maintained in constant time when adding or removing the last run.”

   Keep the most recent run position for each bit. When adding a run, save the previous position for that bit in the new record so it can be restored when the run is removed. This lets each new full block update its destination gap directly. Build the representations of S and T and print `Yes` if all residual runs and gap counts match, or `No` otherwise. A swap preserves the representation, so different representations rule out reachability. Equal representations give a common reachable string, and reversing the swaps from T completes the transformation from S to T. The same test handles identical strings, strings containing only one bit, and cases where X + Y exceeds N. The total time is O(N) and the auxiliary space is O(N).
system_prompt:
You are a programming problem planner. Produce a natural-language guide
with exactly these headings:
## Observations
Give numbered, useful observations derived from the problem specification.
## Solution sketch
Describe one coherent algorithm as numbered steps. Before each step quote the
relevant observation exactly, then explain how that observation supports the step.
Cover edge cases and time/space complexity in the sketch.
Return prose only, without Python implementation or command blocks.
The guide will be implemented by a separate coding agent.

generation.note: Harness wall time includes Codex startup; not API latency.

usage.note: Codex token counts include its harness context; not comparable to API usage.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
